main_text.p: Cintisce, Antiquo : à Latino, ut videtur, ut nos Anttikscbe, & Cntiscen, Antiquis.
Cttir, Venenum an Cffer noftrum, id est Pus?] Sax. eodem sensu αττοπ, & Ατταρene.
Clelendig, Extraneus : & Cllendiga, Advenam : & Clelendis, Peregrinationis] Videatur hîc Kilian. in vocib. Cl-lendo, Cl-lendigb, & Cl-lendigbepo.

Cldi, Senecta: & Creldi, Senium. Nam Cr auget] Saxon. senecta, ylop̄e. Senium autem ylopene : unde noftratium Olo, i. e. Senex ; Clder, Senior ; Cldeft, Antiquissimus : Sax. ylopta, alias ealpa eloerto, (non alder-eldeft, ut Versteganus, perperam) quasi omnium senior.
Crurt, Pavimento : quasi Crt-urif, quòd terram tueatur] Vide Kilian. in voce Cre.
Creve, Hæreditas] Hoc Sax ynpe, enpe, ynppeaponerre? Belg. Crf, Crf-goed, Crve.
Ctoa, Lex : & Cton, Lege. vide Cltat Ctoenlart, Legislatorem] Sax. Lex,

page.notes: Handwritten marks at upper right and a faint mark beside the right column are not printed text and are omitted. Several Anglo-Saxon and Greek words in this page are printed in a blackletter-influenced type and are uncertain; no [?] applied due to the scan quality, but readings such as "Cltat", "Ctoenlart" and the Greek forms are doubtful.
